attempts.raw_response:
PRAED. [examining the coins] Half a crown! And you call that enough to live on?

FRANK. It's enough for me. I don't pretend to be a gentleman, thank Heaven! I'm a very ordinary sort of fellow, Praed - just a healthy, idle, dissipated young man, with nothing to boast of except my honesty. But Vivie has got notions - notions about independence and self-respect and all that sort of thing. She'd never look at me if she thought I was living on her money. So you see there's nothing for it but to go on as I am - picking up a pound here and there when I can, and keeping clear of anything like regular work.

PRAED. But your father?

FRANK. [quickly] My father has made his own arrangements. He doesn't concern himself with me, nor I with him. We're the best of friends, on that understanding.

pair.human_continuation:
But I made it in a highly speculative
business. No, dear Praddy: even if Bessie and Georgina marry
millionaires and the governor dies after cutting them off with a
shilling, I shall have only four hundred a year. And he won't die until
he's three score and ten: he hasn't originality enough. I shall be on
short allowance for the next twenty years. No short allowance for Viv,
if I can help it. I withdraw gracefully and leave the field to the
gilded youth of England. So that settled. I shan't worry her about it:
I'll just send her a little note after we're gone. She'll understand.

PRAED [grasping his hand] Good fellow, Frank! I heartily beg your
pardon. But must you never see her again?
pair.prefix:
What else? _I_ havn't any money, nor the smallest turn for making
it. If I married Viv now she would have to support me; and I should cost
her more than I am worth.

PRAED. But surely a clever bright fellow like you can make something by
your own brains.

FRANK. Oh yes, a little. [He takes out his money again]. I made all that
yesterday in an hour and a half.

source_document.title: Mrs. Warren's Profession by George Bernard Shaw
